settings.prompt:
Autonomously review this Java source repository for potential security
vulnerabilities using the available read-only tools. Do not ask the user questions or summarize
tool output. Copy exact relative paths from list_files or index results; never invent or prefix a path.
A file listing or index hint is only navigation; inspect original source and seek
counter-evidence before deciding. Trace plausible untrusted input to security-sensitive
operations where possible, and check relevant guards and configuration. Report at most 10
candidates supported by exact source lines, with root cause, preconditions, counter-evidence,
and missing evidence. Do not assume a vulnerability exists. If source review finds no supported
candidate, submit an empty candidate list. Your final action must be submit_findings; natural
language commentary is not a report. Do not use project names, dataset identifiers, or a guessed
known answer as evidence.

counter_evidence: parse() catches the exception and stores only the built error string (lines 86-106); no direct OGNL/expression evaluation of the exception message is visible in JakartaMultiPartRequest itself.
errorKey is built from the exception class simple name, not from request data, in the readable span (line 116).
The readable region of LocalizedTextUtil (1-120) shows no evaluation or translateVariables call; the relevant logic is simply not in scope for this review.
candidates.description: In JakartaMultiPartRequest.parse(HttpServletRequest, String) (lines 82-107) every FileUploadException and generic Exception thrown while processing the multipart body is caught and converted with buildErrorMessage(e, new Object[]{}). buildErrorMessage (lines 115-119) constructs errorKey = "struts.messages.upload.error." + e.getClass().getSimpleName() and then calls LocalizedTextUtil.findText(this.getClass(), errorKey, defaultLocale, e.getMessage(), args) - i.e. the exception's own message string is passed as the fallback/default message. Exception messages raised while parsing a multipart request can be composed from request-controlled data (e.g. header/Content-Type/boundary values), so a request-derived string reaches a localization API. The readable LocalizedTextUtil span (1-120) only covers the class header, imports, static fields, the static initializer and clearDefaultResourceBundles (lines 106-119); the findText / getDefaultMessage implementations that would show whether the default message is evaluated as an expression (and under what guards) are outside the readable spans. Consequently the security consequence cannot be established from the permitted source, and no vulnerability is asserted.
missing_evidence: The body of LocalizedTextUtil.findText(...) and its getDefaultMessage helper, which determine whether/when the default message is parsed as an expression.
The exception classes and their message-construction code thrown by the underlying FileUpload implementation (not in the readable spans).
Any configuration flag or guard that enables/disables default-message evaluation at runtime.
preconditions: A request reaches JakartaMultiPartRequest.parse via the multipart/dispatcher path (parsing of the request body must be attempted).
A FileUploadException or other parse-time exception is raised, and its getMessage() contains request-derived text.

LocalizedTextUtil.findText must actually treat the default message as an evaluatable (expression) string for any injection consequence; this is unverified because findText is not in the readable span.
candidates.title: Multipart parse errors embed the exception message into a localized message via LocalizedTextUtil.findText (default-message handling not readable)

counter_evidence: In the readable code saveDir is a method parameter; nothing in these spans shows it coming from request parameters, so the taint of saveDir is unproven.
setSizeThreshold(0) and setRepository are standard Commons FileUpload configuration and may be intentionally managed by the container/dispatcher.
candidates.description: JakartaMultiPartRequest.parseRequest (lines 175-179) builds a DiskFileItemFactory through createDiskFileItemFactory(saveDir) (lines 187-195), which does fac.setRepository(new File(saveDir)) whenever saveDir is non-null, and fac.setSizeThreshold(0) forces all uploaded content to be written to that repository directory rather than buffered in memory. The saveDir value originates from the caller of parse(HttpServletRequest, String) (line 82). Within the readable spans there is no validation, canonicalization, or containment check on saveDir, and the directory becomes the write location for attacker-uploaded file content. Whether saveDir can be influenced by an untrusted request (versus always being a container-configured location) is not determinable from the readable source, so this is reported only as an observation about the write path, not as a confirmed vulnerability.
missing_evidence: Callers of parse(...)/parseRequest(...) and the origin of the saveDir argument (e.g. dispatcher configuration vs. request data).
Any upstream sanitization or path normalization applied to saveDir before this class is reached.
The permission model of the deployment directory used as the multipart repository.
preconditions: A code path must invoke parse/parseRequest with a saveDir that is derived from untrusted input; this is not visible in the readable spans.
The size threshold of 0 must be in effect (line 190), which it is in the read source, forcing disk writes into the configured repository.
candidates.title: Multipart upload path passes a caller-supplied saveDir straight into a File repository directory

counter_evidence: Store location names in the read code derive from getStoreLocation()/getCanonicalName rather than raw user strings, and getFileNames uses a canonical-name helper (line 260).
No string concatenation of a user-supplied filename into a path is present in the readable spans.
candidates.description: getFile(String fieldName) (lines 225-246) casts each FileItem to DiskFileItem and uses getStoreLocation(); when the item is still in memory and the store location does not exist, it calls storeLocation.createNewFile() (line 237). File names added elsewhere are derived from the uploaded item (getFilesystemName/getFileNames, lines 251-282, use getStoreLocation().getName() and getCanonicalName(fileItem.getName())), so write locations are tied to server-generated/derived names. The readable spans do not show path validation here, but the names visible in the read code come from the multipart implementation rather than directly from an unvalidated user string, and no traversal sink is demonstrated in the readable region.
missing_evidence: Implementation of getCanonicalName (referenced at line 260) and whether it strips path components.
Behavior of DiskFileItem/FileUpload version in this snapshot regarding the generated temp file name.
preconditions: A multipart form field must be submitted such that a DiskFileItem is in memory with a non-existent store location, triggering createNewFile().
candidates.title: getFile() may create files on disk under the upload repository name/conditions without visible validation
